transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Dmitri Koval (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Head of ML, Stratagem), Arjun Patel (SRE), Noah Clarke (CTO)

Auto-summary: (auto) talked about p95, concurrency, token/sec, streaming - rough numbers to follow up.

00:00 - Lena Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood, with dmitri our se. can you do quick intros?
00:08 - Maya Li: hey maya here, head of ml, we run fraud models, latency critical for some flows, also batching for backfill.
00:15 - Arjun Patel: arjun - sre, network and infra constraints, we need vpc and kms.
00:20 - Noah Clarke: noah cto, interested in cost and SLA.
00:25 - Lena Ortiz: great, main agenda - latency/throughput targets, hosted vs dedicated/private tradeoffs, and sample benchmarks.
00:40 - Dmitri Koval: quick q - what are your p95 goals and concurrency patterns for inference?
00:48 - Maya Li: for real-time authorizations we need p95 under 250ms ideally, but p50 is often lower. concurrency for that path is ~200 qps peak, but we also have a batch scoring path that's high throughput - 2k qps but can be async.
01:10 - Arjun Patel: also some streaming responses for multi-step scoring where we want partial tokens asap, so streaming latency matters.
01:20 - Dmitri Koval: ok that's helpful. p95 250ms for auth path — are you including tokenization + model generation in that?
01:27 - Maya Li: yes end-to-end from request to first token, sometimes first-token matters more than full completion. we typically do short generation ~40-80 tokens.
01:40 - Lena Ortiz: good, that maps to the common tradeoff - hosted can hit low latency with shared pools but noise can bump p95. dedicated gives consistent p95 and predictable token/sec economics. private gives you network control but extra ops.
01:55 - Noah Clarke: curious on numbers — what token/sec and p95 can you typically deliver for a 7B-ish model with streaming?
02:05 - Dmitri Koval: rough ballpark — on dedicated A100 style or newer, for 7B we see ~150-300 tokens/sec depending on quantization and batching, first-token p95 in the 80-180ms range when pinned and warmed, end-to-end for 40 tokens could be sub-400ms p95. on hosted with multi-tenant GPUs you might see p95 variability, maybe 200-500ms. (transcription note: 'A100' recognized; some numbers fuzzy).
02:40 - Maya Li: okay so to meet 250ms p95 for first token we probably need dedicated or pinned resources?
02:48 - Dmitri Koval: most likely yes for consistent 250ms p95 at 200 concurrency, you'd want dedicated pools and some autoscale headroom. also prefix/KV cache helps if requests share context.
03:05 - Arjun Patel: we have shared context for customers - ~60% of requests share the same 100-token prompt prefix (model prompt history) — how well does redwood do prefix caching?
03:20 - Dmitri Koval: Redwood has KV/prefix cache at the serving runtime — can cache KV cache to avoid re-computing early layers. that reduces effective tokens per request and increases token/sec. for your pattern we could see 30-50% lower per-request latency after cache warm. (note: speaker pauses, slight overlap).
03:50 - Maya Li: what about concurrent token/sec scaling — if we have bursts from 200 to 1k concurrent, how do you handle?
03:58 - Dmitri Koval: For bursts we recommend mixed scaling: dedicated baseline for steady 200 qps and burst capacity (either extra reserved or hosted overflow). we can route by policy. throughput-wise a single GPU can handle X tokens/sec; you'd shard across GPUs. example: 4 GPU dedicated pool could comfortably handle sustained 1k tokens/sec for 7B with quantization, exact depends on seq len and batching. (some numbers generalized).
04:25 - Noah Clarke: any nuance for streaming vs non-streaming path? we've seen streaming add overhead because of smaller micro-batches and more network hops.
04:33 - Dmitri Koval: yes streaming tends to reduce batching efficiency so peak tokens/sec drops; but optimizations like adaptive batching and prioritized streaming lanes help. also you can set a flush timeout to balance latency vs throughput.
04:50 - Lena Ortiz: quick qualification - are you OK with hosted for initial pilot if we provide an SLO and fallback to dedicated for production?
04:58 - Noah Clarke: possible, but we need guarantees for p95 for the auth path; pilot we'd like to reproduce p95 numbers.
05:05 - Maya Li: can you share sample benchmark harness and we'll run tests against our patterns?
05:10 - Dmitri Koval: yes we'll send a harness and also can run Redwood-run benchmarks with your prompt set under controlled concurrency; we'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and tail latencies.
05:25 - Arjun Patel: on security: we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, VPC peering, and audit logs. private deployment would be ideal for compliance, but operations would be heavier.
05:40 - Lena Ortiz: Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integration; Dedicated gives encryption at rest and isolated pools, plus audit logs. we'll attach SOC2 docs.
05:52 - Maya Li: also data residency - some EU customers, can we pin region?
05:56 - Dmitri Koval: yes region pinning is supported for dedicated and private; hosted can route to regionally located pools. there may be setup lead time.
06:10 - Noah Clarke: pricing tradeoffs — what's the cost delta between hosted burst and dedicated reserved?
06:15 - Lena Ortiz: roughly, hosted on demand is higher per-token but no infra ops; dedicated reserved gives 30-50% lower unit cost at higher commit. private has platform fee + infra. we'll send tailored numbers.
06:28 - Maya Li: for benchmarking, what metrics should we capture? p50/p95/p99 for first-token and full completion, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure, KV cache hit rate.
06:38 - Dmitri Koval: yes include per-route breakdown, concurrency ramp tests, cold vs warm cache, and streaming flush time effects. we'll include sample scripts.
06:50 - Arjun Patel: for our auth path it's critical to validate under TLS and through our VPC egress — network hops matter. can you support agent within our VPC?
06:58 - Dmitri Koval: private deployment yes; for hosted we can do secure peering and VPN; dedicated often supports VPC peering for reduced latency.
07:10 - Maya Li: timeline - we want to decide by end of Q2, pilot in April.
07:16 - Lena Ortiz: good, we can propose pilot scope: 2-week performance pilot with your prompts, run both hosted and dedicated tests, and produce a report.
07:25 - Noah Clarke: what about canary/fallback if model variant degrades? we need graceful degradation.
07:30 - Dmitri Koval: Redwood supports automatic fallback to lighter quantized model variants and regional fallbacks. rollouts and A/B are supported.
07:40 - Maya Li: last q — for token/sec numbers can you give examples for a 13B model? our fraud model may migrate to larger model later.
07:48 - Dmitri Koval: 13B is more variable; on A100 or H100 with int8/4 quantization we might see ~60-150 tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length; p95 first-token might be 120-300ms on dedicated warmed. multi-GPU sharding improves throughput but increases complexity. (transcription: some numbers approximate).
08:12 - Lena Ortiz: recap and next steps — lena: send pricing + benchmark plan; dmitri: test harness and perf numbers; maya: share traffic profile and prompt sets. schedule deep-dive next week.
08:25 - Maya Li: thanks, look forward to the plan.
08:28 - Noah Clarke: appreciate it.
08:30 - Lena Ortiz: bye everyone, will follow up.
